one-line thesis: Alldigi Tech executed a strategic pivot in Q4FY26, sacrificing low-margin domestic BPM headcount to drive a 22.3% YoY surge in high-margin Tech & Digital revenue, resulting in expanded EBITDA margins (27.1%) despite flat overall top-line growth. The appointment of CEO Natarajan Laxsmanan signals an aggressive push toward AI-enabled platforms (HRMS V2) and international expansion, with 90% of HRO volume growth now driven by new logos rather than existing client expansion.
financial scorecard: Revenue INR 598.7cr (+9.6% YoY); EBITDA INR 162cr (+25% YoY, margin 27.1% vs 23.7%); PAT INR 82.2cr (flat YoY due to tax/other items); Order Book: 48% international (HRO); Net Debt: Net Cash INR 147.7cr. One-offs: Q4 BPM margin aberration due to one-time leave policy alignment reversals; Currency tailwind contributed 3.3% to revenue growth.
guidance: Revenue: Mid-teens growth expected for FY27; Margin: 1-2% YoY improvement targeted (driven by mix shift & AI); Order Inflow: Strong ACV additions (INR 40.1cr T&D, INR 54.1cr BPM); Capex: Platform development (HRMS V2, AI modules).
order book & pipeline: HRO order book stands at 48% international exposure as of March 31, 2026. BPM pipeline includes large healthcare, international insurance, and collections deals delayed by macro uncertainty now expected to close in FY27.
segment / subsidiary detail: Tech & Digital: Revenue INR 156.2cr (+16.5% YoY), Margin 44%. Processed 191.5 lakh records. 90% of volume growth from new customers. BPM: Revenue INR 442.4cr (+7.3% YoY), Margin ~13-14%. Strategic exit from low-margin domestic FTE work; International mix now 78% of CXM revenue.
growth verticals / optionality: RCM business doubled in FTEs within a quarter; Launch of HRMS V2 (integrated console) and AI-based payroll analytics module to drive non-linear revenue per employee; Targeting step-growth via large global deals in healthcare/insurance.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded 340bps to 27.1% driven by operating leverage in T&D and exit from low-margin BPM. Cost structure benefiting from AI infusion reducing manual effort; Currency depreciation provided incremental margin boost.
capex / expansion: Focused on R&D for proprietary IP: HRMS Version 2 (AI-enabled integrated console) and analytical modules. No heavy physical capex mentioned; investment is primarily in technology development and sales infrastructure for international markets.
capital allocation: Net cash position of INR 147.7cr. Management actively evaluating inorganic M&A opportunities in both BPM and T&D segments to accelerate strategy, though no specific targets disclosed.
risks & watch-items: AI disruption leading to client headcount reduction (management monitors closely); Macro delays in large BPM deal closures; Dependency on new customer acquisition (90% of T&D growth) vs. plateauing existing base; Currency volatility reversals.
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic. New CEO emphasizes 'technology enablement over FTE business,' acknowledging short-term revenue trade-offs for long-term margin quality. Transparent about rationalizing low-margin work.
non-obvious takeaways: 90% of T&D volume growth is from entirely new customers, indicating existing client volumes have plateaued; Revenue growth outpaced payroll volume growth due to one-time configuration charges and higher international realization, not just volume.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| Domestic-only payroll providers face margin compression from wage codes and lack of scale | Unlisted Domestic Payroll Peers | loser | Med | Alldigi's international mix and AI efficiency create a widening moat that smaller domestic players cannot match. |

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

themes.title: Workforce solutions & facility management formalization
themes.need: Formalization, GCC hiring and compliance outsourcing drive staffing and integrated facility-management demand - QUESS/TEAMLEASE on flexi-staffing & GCC enablement; SIS/KRYSTAL/UDS on integrated security + facility management. Headcount additions and wage-bill growth are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: Net headcount additions; GCC/enterprise staffing wins; new FM contract ramps.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- 25-year legacy with deep domain knowledge in BPM and T&D, evidenced by 97.1% revenue retention rate in FY26.
- AI embedment across operations and products, including proprietary Digicollect 2.0 platform and AI-native HCM SaaS, repositioning the company from labour-arbitrage to outcome-led, AI-augmented services.
- Global delivery footprint across three countries with multi-lingual capabilities (11 Indian languages, 12+ international languages), enabling service to 69 markets.
- Strong international momentum with 71% of T&D deal wins from international markets and 61% of ACV from international/MCP opportunities.
